Funnel plot

Source: R/epi-charts.R
phw_funnel.Rd

Compares areas, providers or practices of different sizes against a target (by default the overall value), with control limits that narrow as the denominator grows. Points outside the limits are coloured and shaped, so unusual values stand out without over-reading small areas.

Usage

phw_funnel(
  data,
  numerator,
  denominator,
  label = NULL,
  type = c("proportion", "rate"),
  multiplier = if (type[1] == "proportion") 100 else 1e+05,
  target = NULL,
  limits = c(0.95, 0.998),
  point_colour = phw_colours[["grey_mid"]],
  labels = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per unit (area, practice...).

numerator, denominator

Columns of events and of population (or patients, tests...), unquoted as in dplyr. Strings work too.

label

Optional column of unit names; units outside the outer limits are labelled.

type

"proportion" (e.g. uptake) or "rate" (e.g. incidence).

multiplier

Scale for the y axis: 100 for a percentage, 1e5 for a rate per 100,000.

target

The target value on the multiplied scale. Defaults to the overall value (sum of numerators over sum of denominators).

limits

Two confidence levels for the inner and outer limits.

point_colour

Colour of points within the limits.

labels

Optional named character vector that renames the zones in the legend and in $data, e.g. c("Within limits" = "Gerllaw'r terfynau"). Names are the default zone text and values the replacement. Each zone keeps its colour and shape.

...

Passed to ggplot2::geom_point(), e.g. size = 3.

Value

A ggplot. The units, with a zone column ("Within limits", "Above 95%"...), are in $data.

Details

Limits use the normal approximation to the binomial (for proportions) or Poisson (for rates) distribution around the target.

Examples

set.seed(2)
units <- data.frame(unit = paste("Unit", 1:40), n = round(runif(40, 200, 5000)))
units$events <- rbinom(40, units$n, 0.12)
phw_funnel(units, events, n, label = unit) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Proportion by unit", x = "Population", y = "Proportion (%)")
